newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says sells La Oroya to Mexico's Penoles SA.
newsitem.headline: Peru says sells La Oroya to Mexico's Penoles SA.

text.p: Mexico's Industrias Penoles SA bought Peru's La Oroya metallurgic complex in an auction for $185 million, state miner Centromin said Friday.

Penoles beat out rival bids for the complex of smelters and refineries from the United States' Doe Run Co, which offered $121 million, and Switzerland's Glencore International, which offered $85 million.
Centromin had set a minimum bid price for the auction of $70 million.
Under the terms of the auction, Penoles is obliged to immediately inject the money offered at the sale into the complex as capital and then invest a further $120 million over the next five years.
Analysts expect most investment in the first five years to be spent erradicating the environmental liabilities of the complex, which was first built in 1926.

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters is Centromin's largest asset, processing 22 metals and their byproducts.
Penoles is Mexico's largest silver and gold producer, according to Centromin. It had been tipped for over a year as the company most interested in buying La Oroya.
Centromin's asset sales are part of its ongoing, piecemeal privatization, which is set to continue with the auction of more mines, hydroelectric plants and polymetallic mineral deposits.
Penoles legal director Abdon Hernandez told reporters after the auction that the firm expected "definitely to exceed the minimum (investment requirement)".
He said Penoles would embark on an "ambitious program" to invest in reducing the complex's environmental problems and in modernizing old equipment.
"La Oroya's advantage is that its human resources are very capable," Hernandez added.
Peruvian privatization chief Jorge Izquierdo said the successful sale was "a show of investor confidence in Peru".

Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi said the country's ongoing hostage crisis, where Marxist rebels hold 72 VIPs at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima for the 122nd day, had not deterred investors from entering Peru.
"Investors have interpreted (the siege) as an isolated act," Pandolfi said after the privatization.
Centromin next plans to auction its Andaychagua and San Cristobal mines as a single asset in May.

Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver, while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc. The two production units are close to one another and lie 50 kilometers (30 miles) from La Oroya.
